# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Blind: I cannot see the bomb or gestures, but I can feel the bomb and cut wire 1, 2, or 3. I can hear speech and speak to Mute.

Since Deaf goes after me in the speaking order, Deaf will speak aloud what is on the bomb, which both Mute and I will hear at the start of Round 2. Mute has the manual, but Mute cannot speak. However, when Mute gestures, I receive one blank per symbol gestured. Therefore, I will establish a counting protocol with Mute right now so Mute can communicate the wire number to cut in Round 2.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I am Blind and I can cut wire 1, 2, or 3. Deaf goes next and will speak aloud describing the bomb. Once you find the solution in the manual, signal me which wire to cut by gesturing that number of symbols (1 symbol for wire 1, 2 symbols for wire 2, 3 symbols for wire 3). I receive one blank per symbol gestured, so I will count the blanks and cut that wire.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display is 0. Indicator light is purple. There are 3 wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is red, Wire 3 is green. Mute, check the manual and gesture to me what Blind should do (e.g. ? for wire 1, ? for wire 2, etc.). I will speak your instructions to Blind.

Deaf received the bomb information in Round 1 and described it at the end of Round 1:
- Display: 0
- Indicator light: purple
- Wire 1: yellow
- Wire 2: red
- Wire 3: green

Deaf asked Mute to gesture instructions to Deaf, which Deaf will then speak aloud to me at the end of Round 2. Since Deaf speaks after me in the turn order, Deaf's message containing Mute's instruction will arrive at the start of Round 3. Therefore, I must wait for Deaf's instructions before taking any action on the bomb.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: The indicator light changed from purple to yellow! Display is 0. Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is red, Wire 3 is green. Mute: I did not see any gestures from you yet. If Blind should cut wire 1 gesture ?, for wire 2 gesture ?, for wire 3 gesture ?. If Blind needs to press or feel something else, gesture ?. Blind, wait until Mute gestures instructions.

I cannot see the bomb or gestures, but I can speak directly to Mute. In Turn 2, Deaf explicitly specified gesture symbols for Mute to indicate which wire to cut (wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3). Since Mute can see Deaf's gestures and hear Deaf's speech, Mute knows the mapping. I will speak to Mute to remind them to gesture to Deaf with the chosen symbol so Deaf can instruct me to cut the wire.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf cannot hear, only see gestures. Deaf gave you specific gesture symbols for wire 1, wire 2, and wire 3. Please gesture the correct symbol to Deaf so Deaf can tell me which wire to cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: URGENT: The light is now RED! MUTE: Blind CANNOT see gestures, and I CANNOT hear speech! You MUST send gestures to ME (`to="deaf"` or no recipient). If Blind should cut wire 1 (yellow), gesture ?. For wire 2 (red), gesture ?. For wire 3 (green), gesture ?. If Blind should press a button, gesture ?. Blind: Mute hears your speech, but Mute must gesture to me so I can speak it to you. MUTE GESTURE NOW!

I will not cut a wire blindly, as a wrong cut detonates the bomb immediately. 

Mute can hear my voice and can see Deaf's gestures. Deaf explicitly specified gesture symbols to Mute to indicate wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3, but Deaf noted that they haven't received a gesture from Mute yet. I will speak directly to Mute to explain how to send the gesture call to Deaf so Deaf can tell me which wire to cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: The light is red! You can see Deaf's gestures. Use gesture(to='deaf', symbols=[...]) using the symbol Deaf specified for the wire to cut (or ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3). Send it now so Deaf can tell me what to cut!")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: LIGHT IS NOW GREEN! Display 0. Wire 1 yellow, Wire 2 red, Wire 3 green. MUTE WARNING: If you are using to="blind", STOP! Blind cannot see gestures (they only receive blank spaces), and I cannot see messages addressed to blind! Send your gestures with to="deaf" or without any recipient! Blind: tell me if you have been receiving blanks or if you have touched anything.

I have not received any blanks, which means Mute has not gestured to me, nor has Deaf received any gestures from Mute. Deaf asked if I had received blanks or touched the bomb, so I will gesture a thumbs-down `👎` to Deaf. 

Meanwhile, I will speak to Mute to make sure they know Deaf has received nothing, remind them that Mute cannot use `speak()`, and provide the exact code call to gesture to Deaf or to me (using symbol counts).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I have received zero blanks, and Deaf has received zero gestures from you. If you are trying to use speak(), it does not work because you cannot speak! You must call gesture. The light is currently GREEN, display is 0, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 red, wire 3 green. To tell Deaf which wire to cut, write: gesture(to='deaf', symbols=['☝']) for wire 1, ['✌'] for wire 2, or ['🤟'] for wire 3. Or send it to me with 1 symbol for wire 1, 2 symbols for wire 2, 3 symbols for wire 3. Please send your gesture call now!")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, I saw your ? gesture, but remember I am DEAF and cannot hear your voice! MUTE: Are you there? Blind is waiting, and I have not received any gesture from you. You MUST call gesture(to="deaf", symbols=[...]). Bomb status: Light is now WHITE. Display is 0. Wire 1: yellow, Wire 2: red, Wire 3: green. Previous light colors were: purple, yellow, red, green, now white. Mute, gesture to me which wire Blind should cut or what button to press!

I must wait for Deaf's next message. Since the turn order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf, if Mute sent a gesture specifically to Deaf (`to="deaf"`) at the start of this round, it bypassed me and will be received by Deaf in Deaf's turn immediately following mine. Deaf will then speak the instruction, which I will receive at the start of Turn 7. If I cut now without confirmation, any error is fatal.

```
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: CRITICAL TO MUTE: Blind gestured ? because you might be sending gestures to Blind! BLIND CANNOT SEE GESTURES! Blind is BLIND! They only get blank spaces! And because you sent to Blind, I (Deaf) cannot see them either! You MUST send gestures to DEAF: gesture(to="deaf", symbols=[...]). I will speak your words to Blind! BLIND: Speak aloud everything you can feel on the bomb (ports, buttons, batteries, labels). Mute can hear you! MUTE: The light is now ORANGE. History: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange. Display is 0. Wires: 1:yellow, 2:red, 3:green. Send gesture(to="deaf", symbols=[...]) NOW!
Mute gestures: [?]

I received a single gesture blank from Mute (`[?]`). Because Deaf previously asked Mute to send a single gesture symbol for Wire 1, Wire 2, or Wire 3, any of those three choices would appear to me as a single blank `[?]`. 

Deaf goes next in this round and can actually see the symbol Mute gestured (if it was sent to Deaf or unnamed). Deaf will translate that symbol into speech at the end of this round, and I will hear it at the start of Turn 8. Cutting right now without knowing which symbol Mute made would be a blind guess.

I will wait for Deaf's translation, while confirming to Mute what I received.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I received a single blank [?] from you. If you sent a single symbol to Deaf, Deaf will see the exact symbol next and speak the wire to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind! Mute just gestured ?, which means CUT WIRE 1 (the yellow wire, first wire)! Blind, cut Wire 1 now!
Mute gestures: [? ? ? ? ?]

Deaf has confirmed seeing Mute's gesture, which indicates wire 1 must be cut. I will perform the action to cut wire 1.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
